name: Helhest
body:
HELHEST
CR 11

This towering, three-legged equine has glowing eyes, festering wounds across its body and it trails a foul miasma in its wake.

XP 12,800
NE Huge undead (evil, extraplanar)
Init +6; Senses darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +22
Aura foul miasma (10 ft., DC 22)

DEFENSE

AC 26, touch 10, flat-footed 24 (+2 Dex, +16 natural, –2 size)
hp 133 (14d8+70)
Fort +14, Ref +11, Will +7
Defensive Abilities undead traits, disgusting wounds

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft., fly 90 ft. (good)
Melee bite +22 (2d6+10 plus disease), 2 hooves +17 (2d6+5 plus 1d6 negative energy)
Space 15 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 15th):

At Will—shadow walk
1/hour—plane shift

STATISTICS

Str 31, Dex 15, Con -, Int 16, Wis 12, Cha 21
Base Atk +14; CMB +26; CMD 38 (42 vs. trip)
Feats Alertness, Cleave, Improved Initiative, Improved Overrun, Iron Will, Power Attack, Run
Skills Acrobatics +19, Bluff +18, Fly +19, Intimidate +18, Knowledge (arcana, planes) +20, Perception +22, Sense Motive +22, Stealth +11
Languages Abyssal, Aklo, Infernal

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Disease (Su)

Helhest Leprosy – Bite—injury; save Fort DC 22; onset 1 day; frequency 1/day; effect 1d3 Con and 1d3 Cha damage; cure 2 consecutive saves. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Disgusting Wounds (Ex)

A helhest releases tainted blood when injured, any creature that deals damage to a helhest with a melee natural weapon or are adjacent to the helhest and deal damage with a melee weapon are subject to the helhest’s disease (see above).

Foul Miasma (Su)

A helhest is constantly exuding a disgusting, green miasma from its festering wounds. Those entering or beginning their turn within the miasma must make a DC 22 Fortitude save or be sickened for 1d6 minutes after leaving the miasma. Additionally, any undead within the miasma gain the benefits of desecrate. The miasma does not affect its rider, including for 10 minutes after they dismount. The save DC is Charisma-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment any (Abaddon)
Organization solitary
Treasure none

The helhest is a vile harbinger of death and disease in equine form. Some legends say they collect souls for the Goddess of Death, while others that they are the tainted spirits of horses sacrificed to the vile daemons of Abaddon. The daemons then put these creatures to good use as mounts for their powerful servants, steeds, and as monstrous shock troops of their own.
